To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) activity-dependent neurite growth can cause complex behaviour in neural networks, (2) the behaviour depends on the range of activity over which outgrowth takes place, and (3) this range can vary among cells.
activity-dependent neurite retraction can lead to periodic activity patterns and that this can be explained by the adaptation of any cellular property that adaptes slowly to electrical activity.
activity-dependent neurite growth may lead to complex periodic activity and connectivity patterns in neural networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of how the dynamics of the electrical activity in a neural network can influence the connectivity of the network.
the question how a neural network can maintain its activity at a given level by changing its own connectivity.
the study of the dynamics of neural networks with activity-dependent outgrowth of dendritic and axonal branches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed complex periodic behaviour is a general phenomenon that is not specific to the neurite outgrowth process.
the activity-dependent neurite growth mechanism can be the source of the complex behaviour of neural networks.
the activity-dependent outgrowth of neurites in a neuronal network can lead to a variety of complex periodic behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of neural networks can be strongly affected by the presence of activity-dependent neurite growth, even in the absence of external inputs.
a slow adaptation to electrical activity can lead to complex behaviour in the network, which can be observed in the electrical activity as well as in the connectivity of the cells.

a network of cells with activity-dependent neurites can lead to a complex network dynamics that can be described by a combination of the dynamics of individual cells and the spatial distribution of cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of a network of interacting cells can be affected by the way in which the cells adapt their properties in response to electrical activity.
the spatial distribution and the distribution of outgrowth properties over cells can lead to the emergence of complex dynamics.
a simple mechanism, such as neurite outgrowth, can lead to complex behaviour in the connectivity and activity of individual cells.
